scout.productSummary: A vehicle-routing / logistics engine for the capacitated VRP with time windows (CVRPTW), rebuilt from a sourcing optimizer that is archived at git tag archive/sourcing-v1. backend/app/vrp/ holds one data model, three solver paths (CP-SAT exact, Clarke-Wright savings, OR-Tools routing) and one shared validator every solution passes through; a SimPy discrete-event simulation stresses a route plan with random travel and service times, and a buffer-tuning loop searches schedule/capacity buffers against it. backend/scripts/benchmark_solomon.py writes the committed docs/benchmark_results.json (168 Solomon cases x 3 solvers, gaps vs best-known). The web app has three pages - Route Plan, Simulation, Benchmarks - with no login, served by backend/app/api/routing.py. Every headline figure is produced by a command in the repo and written to a committed JSON artifact.
currentGoals: The front door describes the product that exists: README still opens as 'Electronics Supply Chain Optimizer' with forecasting headlines and a BOM feature table, and does not headline the routing engine or its benchmark

Publish the Solomon benchmark from docs/benchmark_results.json, always against its best-known baseline, and name its weak spots (OR-Tools feasible on only 49 of 56 100-customer cases; CP-SAT's mean gap grows with instance size)
Make the guards run where they gate: ci.yml still passes -m "not slow", so the CI run the deploy waits on never runs the slow artifact pins; repo-tests.yml runs them (PR 20) but does not gate deploy

Decide the sourcing leftovers: the auth, cart, graph, feeds, ml, demand, newsvendor, resilience and fiedler benchmark routers are still mounted but no page uses them - propose archive or keep with evidence, the owner decides
Fix anything broken on the live Route Plan -> Simulation -> Benchmarks flow first, then new ideas that let an OR/logistics/supply-chain recruiter try the strongest true result
A proposal that would move a still-published resume figure (Brier 0.393, rank 1.66) is allowed, but its title starts with [resume-figure] and its body has a before/after table
offLimits: Hand-editing GENERATED regions, docs/*.json artifacts (including docs/benchmark_results.json), metrics.joblib or provenance stamps; regenerate from a clean tree instead
Synthetic, fabricated or live data replacing the frozen 2024 snapshot, drift in backend/seeds/data, or benchmark results not produced by the benchmark script
Skipping, deselecting or loosening any test or gate to get green
Claims on the do-not-claim lists, or any percentage without its baseline
Restoring archived sourcing code from archive/sourcing-v1 unless the owner asks
Loop machinery: claude-*.yml, loop-metrics, .github/loop-config.json, the docs/archive/loop-brief.md path
Hosting or plan changes, an AWS move, spending money, credentials, key rotation, git history rewrites; never put a secret or key prefix in an issue
CLAUDE.md, LEARNINGS.md, .claude/, docs/handoffs/; LICENSE text and the CC-BY-4.0 attribution
lenses: Published-claim integrity: a number or statement on a page, the README or a doc that its committed artifact, the served DB or the live API contradicts.
Checks that cannot fail: a test, CI filter or deploy step that would stay green if the thing it guards broke.
Recruiter's first minute: what someone opening the live site or README sees first, and where it breaks, misleads or buries the strongest true result.
Worth building next: a feature that lets a recruiter or procurement user try the strongest true result themselves, using only the real snapshot.
